scanning, the scanning schematic diagram is shown in the Fig. 2 (e-f).Since the spot diameter was 16 m, the intervals between scanning lines were set to 10 m in order to ensure the material can be removed in time.After drilling, the surface morphology of the holes was observed by SEM,and the results are shown in Fig. 3. The hole circularity and taper angle were calculated using Eq. (1) and (2),and the data are displayed in Table 2.

By observing the hole morphology in Fig. 3 and comparing the data in Table 2, the third scanning path with nested circular scanning (insideout) was the optimal processing path, with the circularity of the inlet and outlet reaching 99.4% and 94.7%, respectively, and the taper angle was also the smallest (3.9–4.9°). As Fig. 3(c) shows, compared with the other three scanning paths, its surface morphology was also the best, and the inlet edge was smooth and neat. For the linear scanning path (Fig. 3(a)), the start and end points of each laser scanning route were located at the edge of the hole, because of the discontinuity of the scanning path,the edge of the inlet was irregular. For spiral scanning (Fig. 3 (b)),because the end of the path was not closed, there was a defect similar to a small tail at the inlet edge. For the nested circular scanning path (Fig. 3(c) and (d)),the two scanning processes with opposite paths lead to completely different drilling results. In the early stage of drilling, the hole taper is larger, that is, the inlet diameter is smaller than the outlet.As shown in Fig. 2 (e), during nested circular scanning from inside to outside, the laser was propagated in the air without any hindrance, and its energy was basically lossless. In addition, the laser ablated the

material from the inside to the outside, resulting in that the ablated debris can be splashed out both from the inlet and outlet. Therefore, the material was gradually removed, and the hole shape was gradually optimized. However, compared to Fig. 2 (e), Fig.2 (f) shown the sanning schematic diagram of nested circular scanning from outside to inside.During the laser axial feed process, since the scanning starts at the edge part of the hole instead of the center part, the material was not completely removed, which caused the laser propagation to be blocked,and the energy cannot reach the bottom of the material, resulting in a low material removal rate. Moreover, the ablated debris can only be discharged from the inlet. With the increase of ablation products, if the debris is not discharged in time, it will accumulate on the hole wall,causing repeated remelting of the ablation product, thereby affecting the hole processing quality, especially the outlet morphology 17]. Therefore, the scanning path from inside to outside can be machined a better hole than the scanning path from outside to inside. Then, in the subsequent experiment, hole machining was performed following a nested circular scanning path (inside-out) and with an axial feed method, as shown in Fig. 4.
